# DzCalendar

> A calendar and scheduler written on Temporal: every event keeps its own time zone, days of 23 h, 25 h or 23 h 30 are shown for what they are, recurrence is RFC 5545, and every change is a serializable command. Vanilla JS, Angular, React, Vue and a Web Component; resources, a timeline, bookable slots, an editor, printing and exports. MIT.

Rules an assistant writing DzCalendar code should keep:

- Moments are Temporal values or ISO 8601 strings with IANA zones — `2026-10-21T09:00[Europe/Paris]`, a date `2026-10-21` for all-day. Never a JS `Date` (it is refused: `date-object-rejected`).
- Every event keeps its own zone; the calendar draws in its `timeZone`. Days of 23 h or 25 h are shown for what they are: the missing hour marked, the repeated hour twice, real lengths said; `timeGrid: { axis: 'elapsed' }` draws them to scale.
- Weekdays are ISO: Monday = 1 … Sunday = 7.
- Every change is a command (`calendar.run({ type: 'event.move', … })`), plain data described by `commands.schema.json`; undo and redo come with it.
- Bad data never throws: an event or a command that cannot be taken becomes a Problem `{ code, severity, path, detail }` (`run()` returns `{ ok: false, problems }`; `kernel.getProblems()?.problems` for the last events loaded), every guess a warning. Options are the exception: `createCalendar` and `update` throw a `RangeError` on one they cannot take.
- Colours are tones (`tone: 'amber'`; the themes have blue, green, red, amber, violet, slate), themes decide what they look like.

## Packages

- `@dzcalendar/core`: Calendar model on Temporal: events with their own time zone, DST-correct days. No DOM, no framework, no Date.
- `@dzcalendar/dom`: DzCalendar in plain DOM: views, rendering, interactions. No framework; wrappers sit on top.
- `@dzcalendar/theme`: An optional stylesheet for DzCalendar, of one family with @tzslot/theme. Plain CSS, no framework.
- `@dzcalendar/rrule`: RFC 5545 recurrence rules on Temporal: wall-clock days across clock changes, elapsed-time hours. No event model.
- `@dzcalendar/ical`: iCalendar (RFC 5545) for DzCalendar: parse and write VEVENTs with their real time zones, and an iCal event source.
- `@dzcalendar/slots`: Bookable slots for DzCalendar: weekly hours and exceptions in the provider's zone, minus what is busy, with buffers, notice, horizon and a daily cap. Pure, browser and Node.
- `@dzcalendar/angular`: DzCalendar for Angular 19+: signals only — signal inputs, model(), output(), a CalendarController of signals, templates for events. Zoneless or zone.js.
- `@dzcalendar/react`: DzCalendar for React 18 and 19: <DzCalendar> with controlled or free view, date and selection, a calendar controller read with hooks, and events drawn by the application's own components (portals: its context kept).
- `@dzcalendar/vue`: DzCalendar for Vue 3.4 and 3.5: <DzCalendar> with v-model:view, v-model:date and v-model:selection, a calendar controller of refs, and an #event-content slot drawn by the application's own components (teleported: its context kept).
- `@dzcalendar/element`: DzCalendar as a Web Component: <dz-calendar> for any page or framework — in the page (its CSS applies) or isolated in a shadow root; attributes, properties and dz-* DOM events.
- `@dzcalendar/pro`: DzCalendar Pro: the timeline (resources in rows along an elapsed time axis, a resource area with tree, groups and field columns, windowed in two dimensions), slot capacity, the event and recurrence editor, paged printing and exports (PDF, PNG, XLSX, CSV, ICS) without dependencies. MIT.
- `@dzcalendar/pro-angular`: DzCalendar Pro for Angular 19+: a dzEventEditor directive on <dz-calendar> (the event and recurrence editor, loaded on its first opening) and the DzExport service (printing, PDF, PNG, XLSX, CSV, ICS, loaded on first use). The timeline views come with `import '@dzcalendar/pro'`. MIT.
- `@dzcalendar/pro-react`: DzCalendar Pro for React 18 and 19: useEventEditor (the event and recurrence editor, loaded on its first opening) and useDzExport (printing, PDF, PNG, XLSX, CSV, ICS, loaded on first use). The timeline views come with `import '@dzcalendar/pro'`. MIT.
- `@dzcalendar/pro-vue`: DzCalendar Pro for Vue 3.4 and 3.5: useEventEditor (the event and recurrence editor, loaded on its first opening) and useDzExport (printing, PDF, PNG, XLSX, CSV, ICS, loaded on first use). The timeline views come with `import '@dzcalendar/pro'`. MIT.
- `@dzcalendar/motion-gsap`: Optional GSAP motion for DzCalendar: presets sober and expressive; zone glides, DST unfolding, the title odometer, month → day morph, drag tilt and magnetic slots, dissolving deletes, overlays from their origin, timeline accordion — reduced-motion aware; plugins given by the application.
- `@dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar`: Moving from FullCalendar: an application's FullCalendar options translated to DzCalendar at run time — views, zones, events and sources, editing, rules, callbacks, resources — with every guess and every option without an equivalent said.
- `@dzcalendar/migrate`: dz-migrate: rewrites a FullCalendar application for DzCalendar — imports and plugins, new Calendar(...), the common calendar calls, Angular's <full-calendar> — and marks what needs a person (// dz-migrate:). A tool: never a dependency of an application.

---

<!-- docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started — `@dzcalendar/core`, `@dzcalendar/dom`

A calendar and scheduler on Temporal: every event keeps its own time zone,
and days of 23 h, 25 h or 23 h 30 are shown for what they are — the hour that
does not exist marked, the repeated hour shown twice, real lengths said (and
drawn to scale with `timeGrid: { axis: 'elapsed' }`). No `Date` anywhere:
moments are Temporal values or ISO 8601 strings with IANA zones.

```sh
npm install @dzcalendar/core @dzcalendar/dom @dzcalendar/theme
```

```ts
import '@dzcalendar/theme/dzcalendar.css';
import { Temporal } from '@dzcalendar/core';
import { createCalendar } from '@dzcalendar/dom';

const calendar = createCalendar(document.getElementById('agenda')!, {
  timeZone: 'Europe/Paris',          // the zone the calendar is drawn in
  locale: 'fr-FR',
  initialView: 'timeGridWeek',       // dayGridMonth, timeGridWeek, timeGridDay, listWeek (import '@dzcalendar/dom/list')…
  initialDate: Temporal.PlainDate.from('2026-10-21'),
  editable: true,
  selectable: true,
  events: [
    { id: 'a', title: 'Consultation', start: '2026-10-21T09:00[Europe/Paris]', duration: { minutes: 45 } },
    // Its own zone: drawn at 17:00 in Paris.
    { id: 'b', title: 'Call Chicago', start: '2026-10-22T10:00[America/Chicago]', duration: { hours: 1 } },
    { id: 'c', title: 'Day off', start: '2026-10-23', allDay: true },
    { id: 'w', title: 'Rounds', start: '2026-10-19T08:00[Europe/Paris]', duration: { hours: 2 }, rrule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE' },
  ],
  onEventClick: (instance) => console.log(instance.event.title, String(instance.event.start)),
  onSelect: (selection) => console.log(String(selection.start), String(selection.end)),
});
```

## What it gives

- **`calendar.run(command)`** — every change is a command, plain data
  (`site/commands.schema.json`; in the published package
  `@dzcalendar/core/commands.schema.json`). It returns `{ ok: true }` or
  `{ ok: false, problems, violations? }` — a refused command never throws:
  `{ type: 'event.move', id: 'a', start: '2026-10-22T10:00[Europe/Paris]' }`,
  `event.create`, `event.update`, `event.resize`, `event.delete`,
  `series.delete`, `series.split`, `series.rule`, `event.repeat`, `batch`.
  A person's drag, resize or menu choice is the same commands.
  `calendar.undo()` / `calendar.redo()`.
- **`calendar.update({ … })`** — what can change live: view, date, zone,
  locale, events, sources, resources, business hours, hidden days, theme…
  A refused value throws a `RangeError` and changes nothing.
- **The header**: `headerToolbar: { start: 'prev,next today', center:
  'title', end: 'reload dayGridMonth,timeGridWeek' }` (a space between
  groups, a comma inside one; `false`: none) and the application's buttons,
  `customButtons: { reload: { text, hint?, icon?, click, active? } }`
  (`docs/behaviors/header-toolbar.md`).
- **Formats**: `formats: { slotLabel: { hour: 'numeric' }, title: (t) => … }`
  — each place written with the platform's options or a function
  (`docs/behaviors/formats.md`).
- **Custom views**: `views: { congres: { family: 'timeGrid', visibleRange:
  { start, end } } }` and more (`docs/custom-views.md`).
- **Dragging in** (`import { makeDraggable } from '@dzcalendar/dom/drag'`): `makeDraggable(card, { event: { title, duration },
  data })` and `droppable: true`, `onDrop`, `onEventReceive` (with
  `revert()`); an event dragged between two calendars, `onEventLeave` on
  the one it left; a keyboard path for all of it
  (`docs/behaviors/external-drag.md`).
- **Render hooks**: `hooks.<element>` — `class`, `content`, `didMount`,
  `willUnmount` — on events, days, hours, "+N", the now line, resources…
  (`docs/behaviors/render-hooks.md`).
- **`calendar.navigate('prev' | 'next' | 'today')`**, `calendar.select(…)`,
  `calendar.refetch()`, `calendar.destroy()`.
- **`calendar.kernel`** — the model without the screen: `getState()` (view,
  date, range, title), `store.snapshot` (events, occurrences),
  `getProblems()`.
- **Bad data never throws**: an event that cannot be read is left out and
  said — `calendar.kernel.getProblems()?.problems` lists `{ code, severity,
  path, detail }` (`missing-start`, `unknown-zone`, `zone-defaulted`…) for the
  last load of events; a source's are in its `problems` notice. Options are
  the exception: `createCalendar` and `update` throw a `RangeError` on one
  they cannot take (an unknown view), and change nothing.
- **Sources** fetched as the calendar moves:
  `jsonSource('api', { url: '/events' })` (sends `start`, `end`,
  `timeZone`), `fnSource('fn', async ({ window }) => […])`, iCalendar with
  `@dzcalendar/ical`.

## Many events

Up to 2 000 events, the `events` option is read, checked and indexed when
the calendar is created. Above that, the calendar does the shown period (and a
week either side) first and the other weeks while the page is idle, nearest
first: it is on screen sooner, and nothing else changes —

- showing a period not loaded yet loads the weeks it needs at once (another
  calendar sharing the store too); reading `calendar.kernel.store` (an
  export, a search, the first drag), running a command or an undo finishes
  the rest first, so they always see every event;
- `setEvents` returns the shown period's report; when the rest is in, its
  problems (if any) come through `onSource` (`{ type: 'problems', sourceId:
  'events' }`, the whole report) and `kernel.getProblems()` holds all of them;
- `await calendar.kernel.whenLoaded()` waits for everything — a fraction of
  a second on a quiet page, longer on a page kept busy (a slice at least every
  second).

## Then

- Frameworks: `docs/angular.md`, `docs/react.md`, `docs/vue.md`, the Web
  Component `docs/element.md`.
- Resources (a column per doctor), the timeline (Pro), bookable slots,
  the editor, printing and exports, motion, languages, theming: the other
  files in `docs/`.
- Moving from FullCalendar: `docs/migrating-from-fullcalendar.md`.

---

<!-- docs/angular.md -->

# DzCalendar in Angular — `@dzcalendar/angular`, `@dzcalendar/pro-angular`

Angular 19 to 22, zoneless or zone.js, signals only.

## Install

```sh
ng add @dzcalendar/angular
```

It adds `@dzcalendar/core`, `dom`, `theme`; puts `dzcalendar.css` in the
build's styles; adds `provideDzCalendar({})` to `app.config.ts`. It asks
whether to add GSAP motion (`gsap`, `@dzcalendar/motion-gsap`,
`provideDzMotion`), the Pro (`@dzcalendar/pro`, `pro-angular`,
`@tzslot/dom`) and an example component (`src/app/agenda.ts`). Without
prompts: `ng add @dzcalendar/angular --gsap --pro --example`.

## A calendar

```ts
import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { DZ_CALENDAR } from '@dzcalendar/angular';
import type { EventInput, PlainDate, Selection } from '@dzcalendar/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-agenda',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [DZ_CALENDAR],
  template: `
    <h2>{{ cal.controller.title() }}</h2>
    <dz-calendar #cal [events]="events()" [(view)]="view" [(date)]="date" [(selection)]="selection" [editable]="true" (eventClick)="open($event)">
      <ng-template dzEventContent let-event="event" let-ctx="ctx"><b>{{ event.title }}</b> {{ ctx.timeText }}</ng-template>
    </dz-calendar>`,
})
export class Agenda {
  readonly events = signal<EventInput[]>([{ id: 'a', title: 'Consultation', start: '2026-10-21T09:00[Asia/Riyadh]', duration: { minutes: 30 } }]);
  readonly view = signal<string | undefined>('timeGridWeek');
  readonly date = signal<PlainDate | undefined>(undefined);
  readonly selection = signal<Selection | null>(null);
  open(instance: unknown) {}
}
```

Settled once for the application:

```ts
// app.config.ts
providers: [
  provideDzCalendar({ timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh', locale: 'ar-SA' }),
  provideDzMotion(() => createGsapMotion({ preset: 'sober' })), // one adapter per calendar
];
```

A `motion` given to `provideDzCalendar` or to a calendar wins over
`provideDzMotion`.

## Everything `<dz-calendar>` takes

**Inputs**: `events`, `sources` (keep each spec the same object), `resources`,
`timeZone`, `locale`, `axis` (`'wall'` | `'elapsed'`), `editable`,
`selectable`, `businessHours`, `weekends`, `weekNumbers`, `hiddenDays`,
`messages`, `theme`, `scheme`, `density`, `displayCalendar`,
`secondaryCalendar`, `availableSlots`, and **`[options]`** for everything
else `update()` takes — `firstDay`, `rules`, `nowIndicator`, `scrollTime`,
`dayMaxLanes` (`'auto'`, a number, or `null`: every event, the weeks grow),
`eventMaxStack`, `allDaySlot`, `displayEventTime`, `eventStyle`
(`'tinted'` | `'solid'`), `timeGrid`, `headerViews`, `contextMenu`… All of
them can change at any time.

**Two-way**: `[(view)]`, `[(date)]`, `[(selection)]`.

**Outputs**: `(dateClick)`, `(eventClick)`, `(eventOpen)`,
`(createRequest)`, `(slotClick)`, `(selected)`, `(sourceNotice)`,
`(problems)`, `(resourceProblems)`, and **`(eventChange)`** — what a person
changed (a drag, a resize, the keyboard, the menu, the editor), not your own
`run()` nor a source's delivery.

**Templates**: `<ng-template dzEventContent let-event let-ctx="ctx">` for the
events (a background event — a closed day — gets `ctx.background`: give it
something to show a label at the top of its column, nothing and it stays a
tint); `<ng-template dzDayHeader let-day>` for each day's head (`day.date`,
`day.resource`, `day.lengthMinutes` — 1 380 or 1 500 on a clock change —
`day.text`, the calendar's own words). Both are your components, in your
injector, checked when your signals change.

The same for every element with a content, `let-ctx` (its context,
docs/behaviors/render-hooks.md): `dzDayCell`, `dzSlotLabel`,
`dzAllDayLabel`, `dzMoreLink`, `dzNowIndicator`, `dzWeekNumber`,
`dzNoEvents`, `dzListDayHeader`, `dzMonthHeader`, `dzResource`,
`dzResourceGroupHeader`, `dzResourceAreaHeader` (all in `DZ_CALENDAR`).
`<ng-template dzHeaderItem="filter" let-ctx>` is your place in the header,
named in `headerToolbar` (`[options]="{ headerToolbar: { end: 'filter
timeGridWeek' } }"`); `customButtons` for plain buttons. `[hooks]` gives
classes and mounts for any element (the holders — a day's column, a
timeline row — too), merged with the templates: the template gives the
content, `hooks` the rest.

**Dragging in**: `(dropped)`, `(eventReceive)`, `(eventLeave)` with `makeDraggable` from `@dzcalendar/dom/drag` on your list's items (in `afterNextRender`, its clean-up in `DestroyRef.onDestroy`) and `[options]="{ droppable: true }"` (`docs/behaviors/external-drag.md`). `dropped`, not `drop`: an output named `drop` would also hear the browser's own drop event.

**The controller** (`#cal` then `cal.controller`, or `inject(CalendarController)`
in a child): signals `state`, `title`, `range`, `view`, `date`, `canUndo`,
`canRedo`, `loading`, `problems`, `instance`; methods `prev`, `next`,
`today`, `goTo`, `changeView`, `dispatch` (a command), `undo`, `redo`,
`refetch`.

## Saving a person's change on the server

```ts
import type { EventChange } from '@dzcalendar/dom';

@Component({
  imports: [DZ_CALENDAR],
  template: `<dz-calendar [events]="events()" [editable]="true" (eventChange)="save($event)" />`,
})
export class Agenda {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  save(change: EventChange) {
    const moved = change.after;
    if (!moved) return;
    this.http.patch(`/api/appointments/${moved.id}`, { start: moved.start.toString(), end: moved.end.toString() }).subscribe({
      // Refused (a slot taken meanwhile): exactly this change is taken back — not "the last one".
      error: () => change.revert(),
    });
  }
}
```

`change.command` is the command that was run; `change.changes` lists every
event and series it touched (`before` / `after`, null when created or
removed). `revert()` returns false, and changes nothing, when the event was
changed again since.

## From FullCalendar options

`<dz-calendar [dzFullCalendar]="calendarOptions">` (from
`@dzcalendar/angular/fullcalendar`, with `@dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar`)
lays an application's FullCalendar options on the calendar; it **composes**
with the inputs and `[options]` — the theme, the zone, a context-menu hook
given there stay. The zone of `provideDzCalendar` is kept when the
FullCalendar options name none (theirs is the browser's). `(fullCalendarProblems)`
lists what was guessed or has no equivalent. See
`docs/migrating-from-fullcalendar.md`.

Check templates with `ng build`, not `tsc`: only the Angular compiler reads
them.

## The Pro

```ts
import { DzEventEditor, DzExport } from '@dzcalendar/pro-angular';

@Component({
  imports: [DZ_CALENDAR, DzEventEditor],
  template: `
    <dz-calendar #cal dzEventEditor (editorClosed)="saved($event)" view="resourceTimelineWeek" [resources]="rooms" [events]="events()" />
    <button (click)="exports.download(cal.controller, 'pdf', 'agenda.pdf')">PDF</button>
    <button (click)="exports.download(cal.controller, 'xlsx', 'agenda.xlsx')">Excel</button>
    <button (click)="exports.print(cal.controller)">Imprimer</button>`,
})
export class Planning {
  readonly exports = inject(DzExport);
}
```

`DzExport`: `print`, `pdf`, `png`, `xlsx`, `csv`, `ics`, `download` — with a
`CalendarController` (`#cal` then `cal.controller`, or injected inside a
child of `<dz-calendar>`) or a DOM calendar. The Pro's modules are fetched
on the first use; each call runs outside the zone and resolves inside it.
Bad input never throws: a result's `problems` say it (`not-attached` before
the calendar exists). `import '@dzcalendar/pro'` once registers the
timeline views.

## Notes

- A content hook (or template, slot) now also receives **background
  events**, in a time grid's columns, with `ctx.background`: return nothing
  for them to keep a plain tint. The all-day row's and the month's
  backgrounds stay tints.
- An event is given with `extendedProps` (an input); read back — in
  `eventChange`, `eventClick`, a template — it is a `CalEvent`, whose own data
  is `props` (`change.after.props.patientId`).
- The day-header hook covers the week, day and month views (a month's
  column: the first date of that weekday), not a list's day headings.
- The change output says a person's change — a gesture, the keyboard, the
  menu, the editor, and their undo / redo (`cause`). A command your code runs
  with `{ validate: true }` counts as a person's (that is what it means:
  checked as a gesture is); without it, it is not said.
- A context-menu hook that returns `null` or `[]` means "no calendar menu
  here": the browser's own menu opens. An application that opens its own menu
  from the hook calls `preventDefault()` on the `contextmenu` event itself
  (the calendar cannot know it did).

---

<!-- docs/react.md -->

# DzCalendar in React — `@dzcalendar/react`, `@dzcalendar/pro-react`

React 18 and 19.

## Install

```sh
npm install @dzcalendar/core @dzcalendar/dom @dzcalendar/theme @dzcalendar/react
```

and `import '@dzcalendar/theme/dzcalendar.css'` once.

## A calendar

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Temporal } from '@dzcalendar/core';
import type { EventInput, Selection } from '@dzcalendar/core';
import { DzCalendar, useCalendarController, useCalendarState } from '@dzcalendar/react';

const events: EventInput[] = [{ id: 'a', title: 'Consultation', start: '2026-10-21T09:00[Asia/Riyadh]', duration: { minutes: 30 } }];

export function Agenda() {
  const cal = useCalendarController();
  const { title, canUndo } = useCalendarState(cal);
  const [view, setView] = useState('timeGridWeek');
  const [selection, setSelection] = useState<Selection | null>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <header>
        <button onClick={cal.prev}>‹</button> <h2>{title}</h2> <button onClick={cal.next}>›</button>
        <button disabled={!canUndo} onClick={cal.undo}>Undo</button>
      </header>
      <DzCalendar
        controller={cal}
        events={events}
        view={view} onViewChange={setView}
        defaultDate={Temporal.PlainDate.from('2026-10-21')}
        selection={selection} onSelectionChange={setSelection}
        timeZone="Asia/Riyadh" locale="ar-SA" editable
        initial={{ firstDay: 7 }}
        renderEventContent={(event, ctx) => <><b>{event.title}</b> {ctx.timeText}</>}
        onEventClick={(i) => console.log(i.event.id)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

- **Options are props**: what changed since the last render goes to the
  calendar. Arrays and objects are compared by their contents, so a literal
  written again each render (`resources={[…]}`) changes nothing. Sources are
  compared by identity: keep them stable (`useMemo`).
- **`initial`**: options read once, when the calendar is made (`firstDay`,
  `rules`, `now`…); later changes to it are not read. A prop that goes back
  to `undefined` leaves the calendar's value as it was (pass the default to
  restore it).
- **`view`, `date`, `selection`**: given, they win, as a controlled input's
  value does — `onViewChange`, `onDateChange`, `onSelectionChange` say what a
  person (or the controller) did, and the calendar goes back to the prop
  unless the parent follows. Not given: `defaultView`, `defaultDate`, and
  the calendar keeps its own. A view or date the calendar refused is given
  back (`onViewChange` with the real one) and not tried again until the prop
  changes.
- **`onEventChange`**: what a person changed (a drag, a resize, the
  keyboard, the menu, the editor) — persist it, and `change.revert()` if the
  server refuses (exactly that change, even after another; false when the
  event changed again since). Your own `controller.dispatch()` is not said.
  ```tsx
  onEventChange={(change) => fetch(`/api/rdv/${change.after?.id}`, { method: 'PATCH', body: JSON.stringify({ start: String(change.after?.start) }) })
    .then((r) => { if (!r.ok) change.revert(); })}
  ```
- **`renderDayHeader={(day) => …}`**: each day's head by your components
  (`day.date`, `day.resource`, `day.lengthMinutes`, `day.text`) — a mark, a
  count, a button.
- **A template for every element with a content**: `renderDayCell`,
  `renderSlotLabel`, `renderAllDayLabel`, `renderMoreLink`,
  `renderNowIndicator`, `renderWeekNumber`, `renderNoEvents`,
  `renderListDayHeader`, `renderMonthHeader`, `renderResource`,
  `renderResourceGroupHeader`, `renderResourceAreaHeader` — each given its
  element's context (docs/behaviors/render-hooks.md), drawn by portals in
  your tree.
- **`hooks={{ dayCell: { class: (d) => d.outside ? 'muted' : null } }}`**:
  classes and mounts for any element (the holders — a day's column, a
  timeline row, the view — too), merged with the templates: the template
  gives the content, `hooks` the rest. New closures at each render redraw
  nothing; a function is read when the element is drawn again.
- **`headerItems={{ filter: <DoctorFilter /> }}`** with `headerToolbar={{
  end: 'filter timeGridWeek' }}`: your components in the header (a node, or
  `(ctx) => …` with the view and title); `customButtons` for plain buttons.
- A background event (a closed day) reaches `renderEventContent` with
  `ctx.background`: return something for a label at the top of its column,
  null for a plain tint.
- **`renderEventContent`**: the application's components, rendered through
  portals in its own tree — its context, state, router and i18n reach them —
  before the browser paints.
- **`useCalendarController()`** gives a stable controller (`prev`, `next`,
  `today`, `goTo`, `changeView`, `dispatch`, `undo`, `redo`, `refetch`);
  **`useCalendarState(cal)`** reads it (`title`, `view`, `date`, `range`,
  `canUndo`, `canRedo`, `loading`, `problems`, `instance`).
- **A ref** gives `{ instance, controller }`. Another `controller` given
  later takes the calendar over (the old one is let go). In what `renderEventContent`
  renders, **`useParentCalendarController()`** gives that calendar's
  controller.
- `className`, `style`, `id`, `data-*` and `aria-*` go on the calendar's
  element.
- **Server rendering**: importing the packages touches no `document` or
  `window`; the calendar is made in the browser only.
- **`onError`**: a value the calendar refused (an unknown view); the other
  changes are applied. Default `console.error`.
- **`DzCalendarProvider`**: `defaults` (zone, locale, words…) and `motion`
  (one adapter made per calendar: `motion={() => createGsapMotion()}`).
- `onEventOpen`, `onCreateRequest`, `onSlotClick` change what the calendar
  offers ("Open" in the menu…): given only while the prop is.

- **`onDrop`, `onEventReceive`, `onEventLeave`** (props) with `makeDraggable` from `@dzcalendar/dom/drag` on your list's items: dragged in from the page, or between two calendars (`docs/behaviors/external-drag.md`).

## The Pro

```tsx
import '@dzcalendar/pro';                     // the timeline views
import { useDzExport, useEventEditor } from '@dzcalendar/pro-react';

const cal = useCalendarController();
useEventEditor(cal, { onClosed: (outcome) => console.log(outcome) });
const exports = useDzExport(cal);
<button onClick={() => exports.download('pdf', 'agenda.pdf')}>PDF</button>
```

The editor takes "Open" and "New event here" through the controller
(`cal.takeOver(…)`), over the calendar's own `onEventOpen` and
`onCreateRequest`, until its component goes. The editor and the exports are
fetched on first use. Nothing throws: a
result's `problems` say what went wrong.

## Notes

- A content hook (or template, slot) now also receives **background
  events**, in a time grid's columns, with `ctx.background`: return nothing
  for them to keep a plain tint. The all-day row's and the month's
  backgrounds stay tints.
- An event is given with `extendedProps` (an input); read back — in
  `eventChange`, `eventClick`, a template — it is a `CalEvent`, whose own data
  is `props` (`change.after.props.patientId`).
- The day-header hook covers the week, day and month views (a month's
  column: the first date of that weekday), not a list's day headings.
- The change output says a person's change — a gesture, the keyboard, the
  menu, the editor, and their undo / redo (`cause`). A command your code runs
  with `{ validate: true }` counts as a person's (that is what it means:
  checked as a gesture is); without it, it is not said.
- A context-menu hook that returns `null` or `[]` means "no calendar menu
  here": the browser's own menu opens. An application that opens its own menu
  from the hook calls `preventDefault()` on the `contextmenu` event itself
  (the calendar cannot know it did).

---

<!-- docs/vue.md -->

# DzCalendar in Vue — `@dzcalendar/vue`, `@dzcalendar/pro-vue`

Vue 3.4 and 3.5.

## Install

```sh
npm install @dzcalendar/core @dzcalendar/dom @dzcalendar/theme @dzcalendar/vue
```

```ts
import '@dzcalendar/theme/dzcalendar.css';
import { DzCalendarPlugin } from '@dzcalendar/vue';
createApp(App).use(DzCalendarPlugin, { defaults: { timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh', locale: 'ar-SA' } }).mount('#app');
```

## A calendar

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, shallowRef } from 'vue';
import type { EventInput, PlainDate, Selection } from '@dzcalendar/core';
import { DzCalendar, createCalendarController } from '@dzcalendar/vue';

const cal = createCalendarController();
const view = ref('timeGridWeek');
const date = shallowRef<PlainDate>();
const selection = shallowRef<Selection | null>(null);
const events: EventInput[] = [{ id: 'a', title: 'Consultation', start: '2026-10-21T09:00[Asia/Riyadh]', duration: { minutes: 30 } }];
</script>

<template>
  <header>
    <button @click="cal.prev()">‹</button> <h2>{{ cal.title.value }}</h2> <button @click="cal.next()">›</button>
    <button :disabled="!cal.canUndo.value" @click="cal.undo()">Undo</button>
  </header>
  <DzCalendar v-model:view="view" v-model:date="date" v-model:selection="selection"
    :controller="cal" :events="events" editable :initial="{ firstDay: 7 }"
    @event-click="(i) => console.log(i.event.id)">
    <template #event-content="{ event, ctx }"><b>{{ event.title }}</b> {{ ctx.timeText }}</template>
  </DzCalendar>
</template>
```

- **Props** for the common options, `options` for everything else `update()`
  takes, `initial` for what is read once (`firstDay`, `rules`, `now`…).
  Arrays and objects are compared by their contents; sources by identity
  (keep their specs stable). Give a new array to change events
  (`events.value = [...events.value, e]`): a `push` on the same array is not
  seen. `initial` is read once; a prop that goes back to `undefined` leaves
  the calendar's value as it was.
- **`v-model:view`, `v-model:date`, `v-model:selection`** follow the
  calendar; a view or date bound without its `update:` handler wins (the
  calendar goes back to it); events: `@date-click`, `@event-click`, `@event-open`,
  `@create-request`, `@selected`, `@slot-click`, `@source-notice`,
  `@problems`, `@resource-problems`, `@error` (a value the calendar refused;
  the other changes are applied, the bindings get the real view back; not
  listened to, it goes to `app.config.errorHandler`, else the console).
- **`#event-content`**: the application's components, teleported into each
  event — its provides, store, router and i18n reach them. A background
  event (a closed day) comes with `ctx.background`: render something for a
  label at the top of its column, nothing (an empty `v-if`) for a tint.
- **`#day-header="{ day }"`**: each day's head (`day.date`, `day.resource`,
  `day.lengthMinutes`, `day.text`) — a mark, a count, a button.
- **A slot for every element with a content**, each given `{ ctx }` (its
  element's context, docs/behaviors/render-hooks.md): `#day-cell`,
  `#slot-label`, `#all-day-label`, `#more-link`, `#now-indicator`,
  `#week-number`, `#no-events`, `#list-day-header`, `#month-header`,
  `#resource`, `#resource-group-header`, `#resource-area-header`.
- **`:hooks="{ dayCell: { class: … } }"`**: classes and mounts for any
  element (the holders too), merged with the slots: the slot gives the
  content, `hooks` the rest.
- **`#header-item-<name>="{ ctx }"`**: your place in the header, named in
  `headerToolbar` (`:options="{ headerToolbar: { end: 'filter timeGridWeek' } }"`
  → `#header-item-filter`); `customButtons` for plain buttons.
- **`@event-change`**: what a person changed (a drag, a resize, the
  keyboard, the menu, the editor) — persist it, `change.revert()` if the
  server refuses (exactly that change; false when the event changed again).
- **The controller**: `createCalendarController()` beside the calendar, or
  `injectCalendarController()` in a component inside it (an event's
  content). Refs: `title`, `view`,
  `date`, `range`, `canUndo`, `canRedo`, `loading`, `problems`, `instance`;
  methods `prev`, `next`, `today`, `goTo`, `changeView`, `dispatch`, `undo`,
  `redo`, `refetch`.
- `class`, `style`, `id` and other attributes go on the calendar's element.
- **Server rendering**: importing the packages touches no `document` or
  `window`; the calendar is made in the browser only (`onMounted`).
- `@event-open`, `@create-request`, `@slot-click` change what the calendar
  offers: passed only while listened to.

- **`@dropped`, `@event-receive`, `@event-leave`** with `makeDraggable` from `@dzcalendar/dom/drag` (in `onMounted`, its clean-up in `onBeforeUnmount`) and `:options="{ droppable: true }"` (`docs/behaviors/external-drag.md`).

## The Pro

```ts
import '@dzcalendar/pro';                     // the timeline views
import { useDzExport, useEventEditor } from '@dzcalendar/pro-vue';

const cal = createCalendarController();
useEventEditor(cal, { onClosed: (outcome) => console.log(outcome) });
const exports = useDzExport(cal);   // exports.download('pdf', 'agenda.pdf')
```

The editor takes "Open" and "New event here" through the controller
(`cal.takeOver(…)`), over `@event-open` and `@create-request`, until its
component goes. Another `:controller` given later takes the calendar over
(the events' content keeps injecting the first). The editor and the exports
are fetched on first use. Nothing throws: a
result's `problems` say what went wrong.

## Notes

- A content hook (or template, slot) now also receives **background
  events**, in a time grid's columns, with `ctx.background`: return nothing
  for them to keep a plain tint. The all-day row's and the month's
  backgrounds stay tints.
- An event is given with `extendedProps` (an input); read back — in
  `eventChange`, `eventClick`, a template — it is a `CalEvent`, whose own data
  is `props` (`change.after.props.patientId`).
- The day-header hook covers the week, day and month views (a month's
  column: the first date of that weekday), not a list's day headings.
- The change output says a person's change — a gesture, the keyboard, the
  menu, the editor, and their undo / redo (`cause`). A command your code runs
  with `{ validate: true }` counts as a person's (that is what it means:
  checked as a gesture is); without it, it is not said.
- A context-menu hook that returns `null` or `[]` means "no calendar menu
  here": the browser's own menu opens. An application that opens its own menu
  from the hook calls `preventDefault()` on the `contextmenu` event itself
  (the calendar cannot know it did).
