<!-- docs/element.md -->

# The Web Component — `@dzcalendar/element`

`<dz-calendar>` for any page or framework (plain HTML, React, Vue, Svelte,
a CMS).

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@dzcalendar/element/define';
  import '@dzcalendar/theme/dzcalendar.css';
  const cal = document.querySelector('dz-calendar');
  cal.events = [{ id: 'a', title: 'Consultation', start: '2026-10-21T09:00[Europe/Paris]' }];
  cal.addEventListener('dz-event-click', (e) => console.log(e.detail.event.title));
</script>
<dz-calendar view="timeGridWeek" time-zone="Europe/Paris" locale="fr-FR" editable selectable></dz-calendar>
```

`defineDzCalendar(name)` defines it under another name (`DzCalendarElement`
is the class); `@dzcalendar/element/define` defines `dz-calendar`.

## Attributes (live)

`view`, `date` (ISO), `time-zone`, `locale`, `theme`, `scheme`, `density`,
`editable`, `selectable`, `week-numbers`, `weekends`, `now-indicator`
(booleans: present, or `"false"`; taken away, back to the calendar's
default). Taking away `view`, `date`, `time-zone` or `locale` keeps the
current value. `shadow` and `stylesheet` are read when it first connects
(the mode is kept afterwards). It is a block (`display: block`); its height
is `--dz-height`.

## Properties

`events`, `resources`, `sources` (live; what cannot be read is a
`dz-problem`, never a throw); `options` (any other option —
`businessHours`, `hooks`, `motion`…). A new `options` object with the same
values changes nothing; a live key (the zone, the theme, `editable`,
`businessHours`…) changes in place, events, edits and undo kept; any other
key makes the calendar again on the same store (events and edits kept,
the undo history not) and fires `dz-remade` (`detail.calendar`: the new
one). `calendar` is the DOM calendar (`run`, `undo`, `kernel`…);
`problems` every problem seen (the last 100). Methods:
`navigate('prev' | 'next' | 'today')`, `update(changes)`, `undo()`,
`redo()`. Properties set before the element is defined are taken.

## Events

`dz-dates-set` (`{ view, date, range, title, timeZone }`, drawn and on every
move), `dz-select`, `dz-unselect`, `dz-date-click`, `dz-event-click`,
`dz-event-open`, `dz-create-request`, `dz-slot-click`, `dz-command-refused`,
`dz-proposal-refused`, `dz-resource-problems`, `dz-problem`, `dz-remade`.
They bubble and are composed (they cross a shadow root).
`dz-command-refused`'s detail is `{ result, command }`. Bad input never
throws: an attribute or a property that cannot be read is a `dz-problem`
(`invalid-option`, `path` like `attribute:time-zone`, `detail` a short code:
`unknown-zone`, `unknown-view`, `not-a-date`, `not-a-list`, `refused`), sent
after the current task (a page that listens once the element is parsed
hears it). At mount, what would leave no calendar (an unknown zone or view,
a bad source) is left out and said; the calendar is drawn.

Three events offer something on screen only when listened to on the element
(or given as a callback in `options`): `dz-event-open` ("Open" in the
menu, Enter on an event), `dz-create-request` ("New event here"),
`dz-slot-click` (bookable slots as buttons). Nobody listening, nothing is
offered that would do nothing.

## With Angular

Use `@dzcalendar/angular` (its `<dz-calendar>` component), not this
element: both use the tag name. In an Angular application that also needs
the element, define it under another name: `defineDzCalendar('dz-calendar-wc')`.

## In the page, or isolated

By default it lives in the page: the page's CSS, a theme, Tailwind apply as
anywhere. With `shadow` it is isolated in a shadow root: the calendar's own
CSS is injected there, the page's does not reach in. Style it then with the
palette (`--tz-*`, `--dz-*`, inherited through the shadow root), a theme
linked in (`stylesheet="/path/dzcalendar.css"`) and its parts:
`::part(calendar)`, `::part(toolbar)`.

---

<!-- docs/resources.md -->

# Resources — one column per doctor, room or machine

A resource is whatever events are booked on. Resource views draw one column
per resource and date; each column shows its resource's events, its own
business hours (read in its own zone), and checks its own rules. Everything
here is in `@dzcalendar/core` and `@dzcalendar/dom` (MIT); the timeline comes
with `@dzcalendar/pro`.

```ts
createCalendar(host, {
  initialView: 'resourceTimeGridDay',
  resources: [
    { id: 'benali', title: 'Dre Benali', service: 'Cardiology' },
    { id: 'haddad', title: 'Dr Haddad', service: 'Cardiology', timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh',
      businessHours: { daysOfWeek: [7, 1, 2, 3, 4], start: '08:00', end: '12:00' }, eventConstraint: 'businessHours' },
  ],
  resourceGroupField: 'service',
  events: [{ id: 'a', title: 'Visit', start: '2026-10-21T09:00[Europe/Paris]', resourceId: 'benali' }],
  editable: true,
});
```

## Views

| View | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `resourceTimeGridDay` | the hours of one day, a column per resource (no row of dates: the title says the day) |
| `resourceTimeGridWeek` | each resource's seven days side by side, under its name |
| `resourceDayGridDay`, `resourceDayGridWeek` | the same as rows of days |
| `resourceDayGridMonth` | each week row holds every resource's week |

They are the time grid and the day grid given resources (`ViewSpec.resources`),
so everything those views do works here: drag, resize, select, the context
menu, the keyboard, "+N", bookable slots, windowing. A custom view takes
`resources: true` too. Resources go first: a resource's days are side by
side (dates above resources is not offered).

## Resources

```ts
interface ResourceInput {
  id: string;
  title?: string;
  parentId?: string;          // a tree: a department above its doctors
  order?: number;             // siblings by this first (lowest first)
  timeZone?: string;          // where its business hours are read
  businessHours?: BusinessHoursInput;   // its own, over the calendar's
  eventConstraint?: ConstraintSpec;     // where its events may go, over the calendar's
  eventOverlap?: boolean;     // false: no two of its events overlap; true: they may
  classNames?: string[];      // on its head
  extendedProps?: object;
  [field: string]: unknown;   // your own fields: ordering, grouping
}
```

- **Order:** depth first, children right under their parent. Siblings go by
  `order`, then by `resourceOrder` (`'title'`, `'-title'` descending,
  `'unit,title'`, or a comparison), then as given. Fields are read from the
  resource, then from `extendedProps`. Numbers compare as numbers, text by
  code unit (the same order on every machine), absent values last.
- **Groups:** `resourceGroupField: 'service'` puts a head over each run of
  resources sharing the value, in the order the groups first come. Grouping
  applies to the roots; each root's subtree stays in its group.
- **Bad input never throws.** `kernel.setResources(list)` (and the
  `resources` option) returns what it could not read — the calendar hands it
  to `onResourceProblems(problems)` (Angular: `(resourceProblems)`):
  `invalid-resource` (not an object, no id — refused; a field that cannot be
  read — dropped with a warning), `duplicate-id` (the second one refused),
  `unknown-zone`, `unknown-resource` (an unknown parent: the resource becomes
  a root), `resource-cycle` (the first resource of a cycle, in input order,
  becomes a root). `kernel.getResourceProblems()` reads them again. A
  `resourceOrder` comparison that throws leaves the input order
  (`invalid-resource` at `resourceOrder`).
- `update({ resources })` replaces them (the same array again changes
  nothing); `update({ resourceOrder, resourceGroupField })` reorders.
- An event goes on resources with `resourceId` or `resourceIds`. An event
  on two resources is drawn in both columns. Events on no resource are not
  shown in resource views (the timeline has an "Unassigned" row).
- No resources at all (none given, or not loaded yet): "No resources to
  show" in place of the columns (`noResources`, `.dz-empty`).
- Slots: `availableSlots` entries with a `resourceId` show in that
  resource's columns only. A resource's `timeZone` is not handed to
  `findSlots`: give the provider's availability its zone there.

## Zones and hours

Every column is drawn in the calendar's zone. A
resource's `timeZone` is where its hours are read: a doctor in Riyadh open
08:00–12:00 is shaded outside 07:00–11:00 in Paris in October, and outside
06:00–10:00 from the 25th, when Paris falls back an hour. A resource without
hours of its own takes the calendar's `businessHours`, read in its zone.

## Rules

Each resource an event goes on checks, in its own zone:

- its `eventConstraint`, else the calendar's `rules.constraint` — and
  `'businessHours'` means its own hours (else the calendar's);
- its `eventOverlap` for the events it shares: `false` refuses an overlap
  even if the calendar allows them, `true` allows it even if the calendar
  refuses them. Events on different resources never meet; an event on no
  resource meets every event.

A refused drop is said and handed to `onCommandRefused` with the violations
(`constraint` with the resource's id, `overlap` with the other event's).

## Moving between resources

A drag from one resource's column to another's swaps that resource for the
new one and keeps the others: an event on Dr A and Dr C, dragged from A to B,
ends up on B and C. A resize keeps the resources. A selection, a date click
(`onDateClick`) and the context menu's "New event" carry the column's
`resourceId`.

## Keyboard and screen readers

- Each column's name starts with its resource ("Dr Haddad, Wednesday
  21 October"); a day grid's cell too. The heads themselves are hidden from
  screen readers (the columns say whose they are).
- Left and right stay in the days of the cursor's resource (past the last
  one, the next period, same resource). **Alt+Left and Alt+Right** go to the
  previous or next resource, the same day and time; past the last one:
  "No further". Page Up and Down change the period.
- Holding an event (M), Alt+Left/Right move it to the next resource, the
  same day and time; plain arrows move it in time, on its resource. What is
  said starts with the new resources' names. Resources replaced while an
  event is held let it go ("Move cancelled"); a cursor whose column went
  away starts again at its home.

## Look

- Heads: `.dz-tg__resource` / `.dz-dg__resource` (with the resource's
  `classNames`, and `data-resource`), groups `.dz-tg__group` /
  `.dz-dg__group`. Where a resource's days start, a 2 px line
  (`--dz-resource-border`).
- `hooks.resource.content({ resource }, el)` (`ResourceContentCtx`) draws a head (a photo, a
  specialty); null keeps the title.
- Angular: `[resources]`; `resourceOrder` and `resourceGroupField` in
  `[options]`.

## Limits (on purpose, for now)

- No horizontal scrolling: forty resources over a week are 280 thin columns.
  Use the day view for many resources, or the timeline (15b).
- No per-column zone (K.6), no dates above resources.
- Events whose resource is unknown are kept but shown in no resource view;
  `unknown-resource` is not reported for them (resources may arrive after
  the events).

---

<!-- docs/timeline.md -->

# Timeline — `@dzcalendar/pro`

Resources in rows, time running along. The axis is **elapsed**: a position is
real time since the start, so an event is as long on screen as it lasts, a
25-hour day is 25 hours wide and a 23-hour one 23. The
slots are cut on the wall clock: on a fall-back night 02:00 happens twice —
the second marked `02:00*`, both named with their offsets — and on a
spring-forward night there is no 02:00 at all.

```ts
import { createCalendar } from '@dzcalendar/dom';
import '@dzcalendar/pro'; // registers the family and its eight views

createCalendar(host, {
  initialView: 'resourceTimelineWeek',
  resources: [
    { id: 'card', title: 'Cardiology', service: 'Medicine' },
    { id: 'benali', title: 'Dr Benali', parentId: 'card', room: 'B12' },
  ],
  resourceGroupField: 'service',
  viewOptions: { timeline: { areaColumns: [{ field: 'title', header: 'Resource', width: 170 }, { field: 'room', header: 'Room' }] } },
  timeline: { slot: 60, maxLanes: 3 },
  editable: true,
});
```

MIT: `@dzcalendar/pro` is a code boundary, no licence key.

## Views and scale

| View | Default slot |
|---|---|
| `timelineDay`, `resourceTimelineDay` | 30 minutes |
| `timelineWeek`, `resourceTimelineWeek` | 1 hour (days above the hours, scrolled along) |
| `timelineMonth`, `resourceTimelineMonth` | 1 day (months above) |
| `timelineYear`, `resourceTimelineYear` | 1 day |

`timeline: { slot }` sets the scale for every timeline view: whole minutes
dividing a day (5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 60, 120…) or `'day'`; anything else is
refused (RangeError, at creation or `update()`), and `slot: undefined` goes
back to the default. A wall-clock slot crossing a clock change keeps its
true width (an hourly slot is 90 minutes wide on Lord Howe's spring day). The width of a slot is the stylesheet's:
`--dz-tl-slot` (2.75rem; 2.25rem counted in days). A timeline is continuous
time: hidden days are not taken out. On first paint (and after another
period or scale) it scrolls to `scrollTime` of today when shown, else of its
first day; counted in days, to today.

## Rows

- **Fixed height, "+N"**: a resource row shows
  `timeline.maxLanes` lanes (default 3); past them its last lane holds "+N"
  links, one per stretch where the hidden events run into one another, and
  the link opens them in the "+N" panel. Every resource row has the same
  height, so windowing is arithmetic.
- **Without resources** (`timelineDay`…): one row of every event, filling
  the view (its lanes are measured).
- **Tree and groups**: rows follow the resource tree (depth first, the
  15a order) and `resourceGroupField` (a head row per group, roots grouped).
  Folding a resource or a group is kept in the kernel
  (`collapsedResources`, `collapsedGroups`), so it survives `update()`;
  `onResourceToggle({ collapsedResources, collapsedGroups })` reports it,
  `update({ collapsedResources, collapsedGroups })` sets it. A day the zone
  skipped is said ("This day does not exist in this time zone").
- **"Unassigned"** (`showUnassigned: true`, default off): a
  first row of the events on no resource or on resources the
  calendar does not know. Dropping an event there takes it off the resource
  it was taken from (the others stay); dragging it out puts it on the row it
  is dropped on. The column views offer it too. It is the view's, not a
  resource: a date click or a selection on it carries no `resourceId`.
- Business hours shade each row in its resource's zone (15a); counted in
  days, a day without any open hour is shaded whole.

## The resource area

- Columns: `viewOptions.timeline.areaColumns` — `field` (read with
  `fieldOf`: the resource's own, then what was given, then `extendedProps`),
  `header` (the title column is "Resource" by default), `width` (px;
  default 160, then 110; 40 to 480). Each head has a separator to drag; from
  the keyboard the separators are one tab stop — ↑/↓ from one to the next,
  ←/→ 16 px a step. A width belongs to its field and is kept while the view
  lives.
- `hooks.resource.content({ resource }, el)` draws the first cell's title.
- The area sticks to the left and the heads to the top of the one scroller:
  scrolled both ways, they follow without script.

## Interactions

Everything the grids do: drag between rows (the resource taken from swapped
for the row's), resize by either edge (from the start with
`eventResizableFromStart`), select a stretch on a row, the context menu
(a moment, or a day, with the row's `resourceId`), undo. Near the scroller's
edges a drag scrolls along time; the period changes only once the scroll is
at its end; the edge zones start past the sticky area and heads. An
all-day event stays all-day (there is no all-day row): it moves by whole
days. Counted in days, a timed event moves by whole days and is not resized
(as in a month).

## Keyboard and screen readers

- The rows are a `treegrid`: each row says its level, its expansion, its
  index; its first cell is the row head, the time its grid cell.
- Two tab stops: the area's row heads (↑/↓ the rows, ← folds or goes to the
  parent, → unfolds or goes into the row's time, Enter/Space folds), and the
  time's cursor — ←/→ along time (`snapMinutes`, or a day counted in days),
  ↑/↓ the next resource, Home/End the row's start and end, Page Up/Down the
  period. What the cursor says starts with the resource ("Dr Haddad,
  Wednesday 21 October, 09:00").
- On an event, every arrow goes to the next or previous event of its row.
- Holding an event (M), ↑/↓ move it to the next resource, ←/→ in time (an
  all-day event: a day a step).
- The repeated hour's slot heads read "02:00*" and are said "02:00
  (+01:00)": the offset, not the mark.

## Performance

Above `virtualizeAbove` events (or 120 rows, or 400 slots), only the rows
meeting the view and a screen around it are mounted, and along time only
what meets the view and a screen on each side; nothing is mounted before
the scale is measured. Measured in Chrome, minified (`npm run
perf:browser`, budgets in `perf/browser-budgets.json`): 500 resources ×
10 000 events, first frame about 20 ms spread over a year (week and month)
and 40 ms all in one week (budget 80); scrolling about 1 ms of script a
frame (budget 8), longest frame one display frame (budget 25 ms). Not
measured yet: a year view with business hours, a drag's validation.

## Without a screen

`@dzcalendar/pro/model`: `buildTimelineAxis`, `buildTimelineModel`,
`updateTimelineModel`, `TIMELINE_VIEWS` — pure, for a server or a native
port; the `timeline-axis` conformance suite checks the axis.

---

<!-- docs/slots.md -->

# Bookable slots — `@dzcalendar/slots`

When can this provider be booked? The engine takes the provider's hours (in
the provider's own zone), what is already busy, and the booking rules, and
returns the free slots. Pure Temporal, no clock read, no DOM: the page and the
server run the same code and get the same answer.

## The case in ten lines

```ts
import { findSlots, checkSlot } from '@dzcalendar/slots';

const rules = {
  availability: { timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh', weekly: [{ days: [7, 1, 2, 3, 4], from: '08:00', to: '12:00' }] },
  duration: 30,
};
const { slots } = findSlots({ ...rules, from: weekStart, to: weekEnd, busy: bookings }); // the page draws these
createCalendar(host, { availableSlots: slots, onSlotClick: (slot) => api.book(slot.start) });
// on the server, before saving (no range needed: it is the slot itself):
if (!checkSlot({ ...rules, busy: bookingsFromDb }, requestedStart).ok) refuse();
```

## Availability

```ts
availability: {
  timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh',                     // the provider's zone: hours are read there
  weekly: [                                    // ISO weekdays, 1 Monday … 7 Sunday
    { days: [7, 1, 2, 3, 4], from: '08:00', to: '12:00' },
    { days: [7, 1, 2, 3, 4], from: '13:00', to: '16:00' },
  ],
  exceptions: [                                // replace every window opening on that date
    { date: '2026-12-01', closed: true },
    { date: '2026-12-03', windows: [{ from: '10:00', to: '14:00' }] },
  ],
  rules: [                                     // rare cases, RFC 5545
    { rrule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=1SA', start: '2026-10-03', from: '09:00', to: '12:00', exdates: ['2026-11-07'] },
  ],
}
```

- An end at or before the start crosses midnight (`22:00`–`02:00`), so
  `00:00`–`00:00` is a whole day; `'24:00'` is the next midnight. A window
  belongs to the date it opens on: an exception closing Thursday does not cut
  Wednesday's 22:00–02:00 after midnight. An exception with `closed: true` is
  closed, whatever `windows` it also has.
- Windows that touch merge: `08:00–10:00` and `10:00–12:00` are one opening.
- Clock changes: a window across a change holds its real length (Paris
  01:00–04:00 on 25 October is 4 h). A time the clocks skip never adds open
  time: a window *starting* in the skipped hour opens as Temporal's
  `compatible` reads it (02:30 → 03:30 on 29 March in Paris), one *closing*
  in it closes at the jump (02:30 → the moment 02:00 became 03:00).

## Slots

- `duration` and `step` are minutes of **real** time. Slots start at each
  opening's start, every `step` (default: the duration), while a whole slot
  fits. Across a clock change a slot keeps its length: in Paris on 29 March,
  01:30–03:00 is a 30-minute slot, and on 25 October 02:00 is offered twice,
  once per offset.
- A slot is `{ start, end }` as ZonedDateTimes in the provider's zone;
  `slot.start.withTimeZone(clientZone)` shows it to the client. The calendar
  draws it in its own zone.
- `from`/`to`: only slots wholly inside. They never shift the grid (a range
  starting at 09:30 does not create a 09:30 slot): an opening that began
  before the range counts from its true start, looked for up to a week back.
  An opening that never closes (around the clock) has no start to count
  from: its slots fall on multiples of the step since the epoch.
- `duration` and `step`: whole minutes are expected, from 1 minute to a year.
  At most 10 000 slots are returned (and 200 000 starts looked at), with a
  `too-many-occurrences` warning beyond: narrow the range.

## Rules

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `busy: [{ start, end, kind? }]` | Taken time. `kind: 'booking'` (default) gets the buffers and counts toward `maxPerDay`; `'block'` (leave, another agenda) only takes its time. |
| `bufferBefore`, `bufferAfter` | Minutes kept free around each appointment. Two bookings end up `bufferAfter + bufferBefore` apart. |
| `minNotice` | No start sooner than this many minutes after `now`. |
| `maxAdvanceDays` | No start later than `now` plus this many days, at the same wall time in the provider's zone (a whole number). |
| `maxPerDay` | At most this many bookings starting on one of the provider's dates; a full date offers nothing (a whole number). |
| `now` | Needed by `minNotice` and `maxAdvanceDays`: the engine never reads a clock. |

Capacity (several seats per slot) is in `@dzcalendar/pro/slots` (simple
seats):

```ts
import { findSlots, checkSlot } from '@dzcalendar/pro/slots';
findSlots({ ...rules, capacity: 8, busy: bookings }); // slots with `seats` left
checkSlot({ ...rules, capacity: 8, busy: bookings }, start); // … or { ok: false, reason: 'full' }
```

- A booking takes 1 seat, or its `seats` (a whole number ≥ 1; another value
  is a warning and counts 1). A `block` takes the whole slot.
- A slot is offered while a seat remains: the most seats taken at once in it
  (with the buffers, as here) is below `capacity`. Back-to-back bookings
  share a seat.
- `maxPerDay` counts bookings, not seats. Refusals keep this engine's order
  (`notice`, `advance`, `daily-cap`, `busy` for a block), then `full`.
- With `capacity: 1` and no `seats`, the same answer as this package.
- The calendar shows the seats left beside a slot's time ("10:00 · 2 places")
  and says them; a slot's `seats` field is what it reads.

- Bad input is a Problem as in this package: `capacity`, `maxPerDay`, the
  buffers and a `busy` that is not a list refuse the query; an unreadable
  booking is a warning at its own place (`busy[3]`).

Seats from calendar events and resources:

```ts
import { resourceSeats, seatedBusyFromEvents } from '@dzcalendar/pro/slots';
seatedBusyFromEvents(events, zone); // a timed event's extendedProps.seats is its seats
findSlots({ ...rules, ...resourceSeats(room, events, zone) }); // the room's extendedProps.capacity, its own bookings
```

`busyFromEvents(events, zone)` turns calendar events into busy time: events
with `busy` (the default unless `status: 'cancelled'`); timed ones are
bookings, all-day ones block their dates in the provider's zone.

## Checking on the server

`checkSlot(query, start)` answers `{ ok: true, slot }` or
`{ ok: false, reason }` with `reason` one of `invalid-query` (with
`problems`: why), `out-of-range`, `closed`, `misaligned`, `notice`,
`advance`, `daily-cap`, `busy` (the first rule broken, in that order). `from`
and `to` are optional here: without them the range is the slot itself. It
accepts exactly what `findSlots` offers — checked on random queries over the
nine zones of the project's tests.

## Bad input

Nothing throws, whatever the shape (JSON from a database included).
`findSlots` returns `{ slots, problems }`:
`unknown-zone` and `invalid-slot-query` (errors: no slots), and warnings for
what was skipped — `invalid-availability` (a window or date that cannot be
read), `invalid-rrule`, a busy entry that cannot be read. Each problem has a
`path` (`availability.weekly[1]`).

## In the calendar

```ts
createCalendar(host, {
  initialView: 'timeGridWeek',
  availableSlots: findSlots(query).slots,          // any { start, end } list works
  onSlotClick: (slot) => { /* the slot as given: book it */ },
});
cal.update({ availableSlots: findSlots(query).slots }); // after a booking
```

- Week and day views draw each slot as a button at its time (`.dz-slot`,
  tokens `--dz-slot-bg`, `--dz-slot-hover-bg`, `--dz-slot-border`,
  `--dz-slot-fg`), under the events. A slot is cut to the hours shown (one
  from before `slotMin` shows its visible part); where slots overlap (a step
  shorter than the duration) each is drawn down to the next start, so every
  start keeps a part of its own. Month and list views do not show slots.
- Slots must be Temporal values (`Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, as `findSlots`
  gives them); anything else is skipped.
- The calendar creates nothing: `onSlotClick` hands the slot back — the very
  object given, extra fields included; the application books it, its server
  checks it again.
- Without `onSlotClick` the slots only show the free time: they are marked
  disabled, and a click or a drag on one acts as on empty time (date click,
  selection). With it, a drag cannot start on a slot (it is a button).
- Keyboard: slots are out of the tab order (the grid keeps one tab stop). The
  cursor says "Free slot, 10:00–10:30" where it stands in one, and Enter (or
  Space) books it instead of a date click. The cursor moves by `snapMinutes`:
  a slot shorter than that, or off its grid, may be passed over — keep slots
  on the snap grid.
- Words: "slot" in `slotMinutes`, `slotMin` and the cursor's hits is a row of
  the time grid; a bookable slot is `availableSlots` / `onSlotClick`.
- Angular: `[availableSlots]` and `(slotClick)`.
- `playground/slots.html`: a provider in Riyadh seen from Paris, Riyadh or
  Chicago; a click books and re-checks.

---

<!-- docs/editor.md -->

# The event editor — `@dzcalendar/pro/editor`

A ready-made editor: a modal dialog with the usual
recurrences. It opens on an event, an occurrence of a series, or a new
event; it saves through the calendar's history (checked against its rules,
undoable with Ctrl+Z) and resolves with what happened.

```ts
import { editorHandlers, openEventEditor } from '@dzcalendar/pro/editor';

cal.update(editorHandlers(cal)); // "Open" and "New event here" (context menu) open it
const outcome = await openEventEditor(cal, { instance }); // 'saved' | 'deleted' | 'cancelled'
await openEventEditor(cal, { create: { allDay: false, start: instant, resourceId: 'r1' } });
```

Angular: `<dz-calendar dzEventEditor (editorClosed)="…">` (`@dzcalendar/pro-angular`).
It takes over `onEventOpen` and `onCreateRequest`.

## What it edits

- **Title**, **when** — tzslot's `createDateTimeRange`: both ends on the
  event's zone, the measured length (a night across a clock change says
  its real hours), the repeated hour, whole days (its own switch) — the
  **zone** (the event's wall clock; changing it keeps the moments),
  **resources** (when the calendar has some), **colour** (a tone).
- **Repeats**: does not repeat; every N days, weeks (on chosen weekdays),
  months (on the day, on the n-th weekday — "the 3rd Wednesday" — or the
  last one), years; ends never, on a date (that whole day, inclusive) or
  after N times. A rule beyond that (hours, set positions, several rules) is
  shown as written, "custom", and kept unless another is picked. WKST is
  the calendar's (a rule created here takes the locale's first day).
- **An occurrence**: "this event / this and following / all events" (the
  calendar's words). The repeat belongs to the series: it shows with "all
  events" only. "All events" with another rule → the series takes it
  (`series.rule` command: excluded dates and moved occurrences kept, its
  own WKST too); moved at the same time, the new rule moves with it (a
  Wednesday rule moved to Thursday repeats on Thursdays). With "does not
  repeat" → the series stops: its first occurrence becomes the event (same
  id, every field kept), moved occurrences stand alone. A single event made
  to repeat keeps its id and every field (`event.repeat` command).
- A rule read another way (its own WKST, `COUNT` instead of a date…) is
  compared as a form, not as text: saving a title does not rewrite it.
  Nothing changed → nothing is written (no empty change of an occurrence).
- A flight's end keeps its own zone (Paris → Tokyo) unless the zone is
  changed in the dialog.
- "This and following" with another rule is not offered: the repeat shows
  with "all events" only (a split series is `event.update` with
  `scope: 'following'`, which keeps the rule).
- Only what changed is sent: a title edited on an event that already
  overlaps another is not refused for its times.
- Checked before saving: a start and an end, a whole interval and count
  (1 or more), at least one weekday, a last date given and not before the
  first. The message is said in the dialog, the field marked
  (`aria-invalid`) and focused.
- A refusal of the rules (constraint, overlap, a resource's own rules,
  `allow`) is said in the dialog, which stays open. A series is checked on
  its occurrences (a year of them, 500 at most), not only its first: a
  daily rule landing on a booked day is refused. A problem code is said in
  words (`problem(code)`).

## Accessibility

`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, named by its heading; the title takes the
focus, Tab stays inside (and a focus that leaves for the page comes back;
tzslot's pickers, opened on the body, count as inside). Escape cancels —
not while one of tzslot's pickers is open: Escape closes the picker. A
click outside cancels an untouched form only. The focus goes back to where
it was; opened from the context menu, to the event. The refusal is a
`role="alert"`.

One editor per calendar: a second `openEventEditor` returns the one already
open. Destroying the calendar closes it (`cal.onDestroy`, new in
`@dzcalendar/dom`).

Known upstream: tzslot's date fields carry `aria-haspopup` on a textbox (an
axe "aria-allowed-attr" finding) — to fix in tzslot; the browser check
leaves `.tz-dtr` out and checks the rest of the dialog in full.

## Words and look

`editorMessagesFor(locale)` — English, French, Arabic, Spanish, German;
`defineEditorLocale` adds one; `messages` overrides some. tzslot's widget
has its own words in English, French and Arabic: under Spanish or German its
few labels (the length, "all day") are in English until tzslot has them.
The look reads the calendar's palette (the page's `--tz-*` first, as
`.dz-cal`) and hands it to tzslot's widget and pickers; `EDITOR_CSS` under
`injectStyles: false`.

Size: 10.3 kB gzip; with tzslot's widget, 36.4 kB — what opening the editor
costs. `@tzslot/dom` is an optional peer dependency (install it with the
editor); `@dzcalendar/pro-angular` fetches the editor on its first opening,
not with the application.

---

<!-- docs/export.md -->

# Printing and exports — `@dzcalendar/pro/print`, `@dzcalendar/pro/export`

No dependency: the PDF, the zip of an XLSX and its XML,
the CSV and the iCalendar text are written here; each sub-entry is loaded
on demand. Bad input never throws: a result carries `problems`
(`invalid-export`: an unknown view, a range ending before it starts, a
paper that is not `a4`, `letter` or `a3`).

## Paged printing

```ts
import { printPages } from '@dzcalendar/pro/print';
await printPages(cal); // the period shown, A4 landscape (portrait for a list)
await printPages(cal, { view: 'timeGridWeek', from, to, paper: 'letter', orientation: 'portrait' });
```

Real sheets in the DOM, then `window.print()`: a copy of the calendar per
period (a day, a week, a month; a multi-month view prints a month a sheet),
sharing its store (nothing fetched again), with the period's title and
"n / of". A copy has the calendar's look and options but none of its
handlers, motion or context menu; paper is light, whatever the scheme on
screen. One print job per document: a second call, or
the calendar destroyed, closes the first. What a sheet cannot hold is a
`clipped:n` warning; a date range that could not be fetched, a `sources`
warning. The browser draws the text: any script, selectable in "Save as
PDF". Each copy is sized to its sheet: a time grid's hours fill its height,
a month's weeks too, a timeline's day its width (a slot coarse enough to be
labelled: an hour, two…). A resource timeline is split between sheets by
whole top-level resources (`rowsPerPage`, default what the sheet holds).
No "now" line on paper. `print: false` builds the sheets and returns them
(`job.pages`) without printing; `job.close()` takes them away (done after
printing by itself).

## PDF and PNG

```ts
import { exportPDF, exportPNG, download } from '@dzcalendar/pro/export';
const { blob, problems } = await exportPDF(cal, { from, to, paper: 'a4' });
if (blob) download(blob, 'agenda.pdf');
const { blobs } = await exportPNG(cal, { scale: 2 }); // a PNG per sheet
```

Every view is drawn from its model on a canvas — time grid (with
resources), month, list (over as many sheets as it takes, a day's head
repeated), timeline (rows over several sheets, heads repeated). Days of 23
and 25 hours as they are: a repeated hour striped on the wall axis, a
timeline day 25 hours wide. Right to left in Arabic and Hebrew; each text
in its own direction. The PDF holds the sheets as images (the browser
shapes every script): text is not selectable, about
150–300 kB a sheet at `scale: 2` (192 dpi). The colours are the calendar's
light palette (`--dzc-*`, `--dz-tone-*`), whatever the scheme on screen.
Sheets are drawn and encoded one at a time on one canvas; at most 60
periods and 300 sheets (past them, a `cut:n` warning).

The drawing is plain data: `paintSheets(kernel, periods, …)` gives each
sheet's operations (`Pen.ops`: rectangles, lines, text, stripes), drawn by
`drawSheet(canvas, ops, …)` — testable without a browser.

## XLSX and CSV

```ts
const { blob } = await exportXLSX(cal, { from, to });
await exportCSV(cal, { separator: ';' }); // a French Excel
```

A row per occurrence (series expanded, each once), in order: title; start
**in the event's zone** and that zone; end **in its own zone** and that zone
(a flight Paris → Tokyo ends at 07:00, Asia/Tokyo); start and end **in the
calendar's zone**; the real duration in minutes (a night across a clock
change says 420 for 00:00–06:00); all day; resources (their titles);
status. Excel has no date before 1900: such a time is written as text
(1 January 1900 is 1; from 1 March 1900, Excel's phantom 29 February
counted). XLSX cells are real Excel dates (wall times: what the cell says is
what that zone's clock said), the head row frozen and filtered, the sheet
right to left in Arabic. The CSV is UTF-8 with a BOM and CRLF; a title
starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is written as text (no formula).

## ICS

`exportICS(cal, { from, to })`: what the range shows — an event as it is,
a series whole (its rule, its moved occurrences) — each in its own zone,
with its VTIMEZONE (`@dzcalendar/ical`). `all: true` writes everything.

## Words

Column heads, statuses, "n / of": `exportMessagesFor(locale)` in English,
French, Arabic, Spanish, German; `defineExportLocale`; `messages` over them.

---

<!-- docs/motion.md -->

# Motion — `@dzcalendar/dom` hooks, `@dzcalendar/motion-gsap`

Three levels:

- **Nothing to install:** a light Web Animations base, the default — the
  period slides its way, new events fade in, a menu or a "+N" panel opens.
  Transform and opacity only; nothing where `Element.animate` is missing.
- **`motion: createGsapMotion()`** (`@dzcalendar/motion-gsap`, GSAP 3.13+
  as the application's own dependency): everything below.
- **`motion: NO_MOTION`:** nothing moves.

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, nothing moves at any level (and
the setting is followed if it changes while the page is open). GSAP is
never in `@dzcalendar/dom` (a test checks it). Nothing is ever hidden with
`visibility` (opacity only): a focused event keeps the focus. One adapter
may serve several calendars in turn; `update({ motion })` swaps it (the old
one's animations finish first); `NO_MOTION` turns everything off.

```ts
import { createGsapMotion } from '@dzcalendar/motion-gsap';
createCalendar(el, { motion: createGsapMotion() }); // "sober"
createCalendar(el, { motion: createGsapMotion({ preset: 'expressive', zone: 0.9, effects: { odometer: false } }) });
```

## Presets

| | sober (default) | expressive |
|---|---|---|
| feel | soft curves, 200–350 ms, no bounce | springs, a little squash, bounces |
| a period | 0.30 s, slides 4 % | 0.42 s, 7 % |
| a zone change | 0.50 s | 0.70 s |
| month → day | 0.42 s | 0.55 s |

Any value of `MotionPreset` (`view`, `enter`, `drop`, `zone`, `morph`,
`odometer`, `dst`, `slide`, `ease`, `move`, `settle`, `pop`, `stagger`,
`tilt`, `leave`) can be given over the preset.

## Effects (each on by default, `effects: { name: false }` turns one off)

- **`zone`** — the calendar's zone changes (and nothing else: the same
  view and dates): every event that moves glides from its old place to its
  new one — 150 at most. The instant stays; only the wall clock it is read
  on moves. Events that appear (another day now) fade in. A second change
  mid-glide carries on from where the events are seen.
- **`dst`** — a day with a clock change comes into view: its repeated hour
  (a 25-hour day, wall axis) unfolds, its skipped hour folds in, and the
  day's "25 h" note pops.
- **`now`** — once a minute the "now" line glides to its new place (in
  its column: a scroll is not a move) with a soft pulse, every minute.
- **`morph`** — from a grid of day cells (a month, a year's month) to a
  single day: the day opens out of its cell (when the cell is on screen),
  its events settling in.
- **`odometer`** — on a move of dates or views, the title's changed words
  roll up (forward) or down (back); with other words altogether the title
  rolls whole. The title itself already says the new words for assistive
  technology; only a copy marked `aria-hidden` (`data-dz-roll`) rolls over
  it. A new locale or zone simply says its words.
- **`today`** — "today" from more than six weeks away: a long, fast run
  that way, then a soft stop.
- **`depth`** — the day heads travel half the body's way when a period
  slides.

- **`drag`** — a moved event leans with the gesture's speed (3° sober, 9°
  expressive) and glides from slot to slot instead of snapping; a resize
  does not lean. Dropped, it settles; thrown (with `InertiaPlugin`), it
  lands with the speed it was let go with. Refused, it says "no", turns
  upright and goes back.
- **`leave`** — a deleted event (or occurrence) dissolves: the calendar
  hands the motion a copy of it as it was (`.dz-leave` layer, no ids,
  `aria-hidden`). Undone within a minute, it gathers back.
- **`enter`** — an event made from a selection pours out of it; new events
  otherwise arrive as a wave (a third of a second at most).
- **`overlay`** — a context menu grows out of the point it was opened at, a
  "+N" panel out of its link (its events cascading in), the editor out of
  the event (or the selection) — and closes back into it.
- **`seats`** — a slot's seats left roll and pop when a booking changes
  them.
- **`scroll`** — "today" from another date scrolls the hours (or the
  timeline) to now: eased, and stopped by the person's own wheel, touch or
  key. The scroll itself happens without motion too (a behaviour of the
  calendar since 17b).
- **`rows`** — a timeline's group or parent folding or unfolding: the rows
  that stay slide, the rows that open unroll (the rows that close go at
  once).

Plugins are the application's: `createGsapMotion({ plugins:
{ InertiaPlugin, ScrollToPlugin } })`. Without `InertiaPlugin` a drop simply
settles; without `ScrollToPlugin` the scroll properties are tweened
directly.

## Writing an adapter

`MotionAdapter` (all optional): `beforeChange(change)` — the old screen is
still drawn, return what you need of it — then `afterChange(state, change,
body)` once redrawn (return `true` when you animated the change yourself:
`viewChange` and `eventsEnter` are then not called for it);
`titleChange(title, from, to, change)`; `nowTick(nodes)`;
`eventsEnter(nodes, { cause, from? })`; `eventsLeave(copies, info)` (return
a promise: the copies are removed when it settles, or after 2 s) with
`wantsLeave()` (false: nothing is captured); `seatsChange(nodes)`;
`scroll(el, { top, left })` (true: you move it; views use the toolkit's
`scrollEased`); `overlayOpen(el, origin?)`, `overlayClose(el, origin?)`
(the editor waits for it); `dragStart(ghosts, kind)` (the live array;
places in `--gx` / `--gy`); `viewChange`,
`eventsEnter`, `dragStart`, `dropRejected`, `captureLayout` /
`animateLayout` (FLIP), `dropSettle`, `overlayOpen`, `destroy`.
`MotionChange` says the causes (`navigate`, `view`, `zone`, `locale`…), the
direction, and the view, family, date, zone and title before and after.
Every state change comes through (`options` and `resources` too, after a
measure): pick by `causes`. Several changes before one paint arrive as one.
Never change text or layout properties: the calendar's places are custom
properties its CSS reads.

---

<!-- docs/i18n.md -->

# Languages

Two kinds of words appear in a calendar.

- **Dates, months, weekdays, times, numbers**: from the browser's `Intl`, in
  every language, with no import. `locale: 'ja-JP'` writes Japanese dates
  today. The calendar turns right to left by itself for Arabic, Hebrew,
  Persian and Urdu (from the locale's text direction).
- **The calendar's own words** — "Today", "+3 more", the context menu, what a
  screen reader is told: English and French are built in; Arabic, Spanish and
  German are one import each, paid for only when imported:

```ts
import '@dzcalendar/dom/locales/ar';   // also: …/locales/es, …/locales/de
createCalendar(host, { locale: 'ar-SA' });
```

A locale is found by its exact tag (`ar-SA`), then its language (`ar`), else
English. Unicode extensions (`ar-SA-u-ca-islamic-umalqura`) do not change the
words.

## Changing a few words

`messages` takes only what changes; the rest stays the locale's:

```ts
createCalendar(host, { locale: 'fr-FR', messages: { today: 'Ce jour', noEvents: 'Rien de prévu' } });
calendar.update({ messages: { today: 'Maintenant' } });
```

## Another language, or a region's own wording

```ts
import { EN, defineLocale } from '@dzcalendar/dom';

defineLocale('pt', { ...EN, today: 'Hoje', previous: 'Anterior', next: 'Próximo' /* … */ });
defineLocale('de-CH', { ...DE, today: 'Hüt' });   // a region: wins over `de` for de-CH
```

`defineLocale` also takes a function of the full locale, called once per
locale: numbers then follow it — `ar-SA` counts in Arabic-Indic digits like its
dates, `ar-SA-u-nu-latn` in Latin ones. The built-in `ar`, `es` and `de` are
such functions (`messagesAr(locale)`…; `AR`, `ES`, `DE` are their words for the
bare language).

```ts
defineLocale('pt', (locale) => {
  const n = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale);
  return { ...EN, today: 'Hoje', moreLink: ({ count }) => `+${n.format(count)} mais` /* … */ };
});
```

`DzMessages` lists every key; TypeScript says when one is missing. Keys that
take parameters are functions — counts go through `Intl.PluralRules` and
`Intl.NumberFormat` for the language (the Arabic file shows the six plural
forms and the isolation of left-to-right fragments such as times, with
U+2068 … U+2069, inside right-to-left sentences).

`messagesForLocale(locale)` returns the words the calendar would use.

---

<!-- docs/theming.md -->

# Theming DzCalendar

A calendar that looks right with one import, and that an application can
change entirely without fighting it.

## 1. Use it as it is

```ts
import '@dzcalendar/theme/dzcalendar.css';
createCalendar(host, { theme: 'slate', scheme: 'auto', density: 'comfortable' });
```

- `theme`: `'standard'` (default), `'slate'`, `'night'`, `'pastel'`, `'frost'`,
  `'solar'`, `'contrast'`, or one of your own (`defineTheme`). Every family has
  a light and a dark palette, all checked for WCAG AA contrast by axe in
  Chrome; `contrast` is the high-contrast family.
- `scheme`: `'auto'` follows the system (`prefers-color-scheme`), `'light'` or
  `'dark'` forces it.
- `density`: `'compact'`, `'comfortable'`, `'spacious'` — the height of a
  minute (0.8, 1.2 and 1.6 px: 48, 72 and 96 px an hour), of a bar, the
  type size. Any other scale: `--dz-minute` (`.agenda { --dz-minute: 2px; }`
  for 120 px an hour).
- `eventStyle`: `'tinted'` (the default: a tint of the event's tone, its
  edge in the tone) or `'solid'` (a block of the tone, its text in the
  page's background colour — contrast holds in light and dark schemes).
- All three change live: `cal.update({ theme: 'night', scheme: 'dark' })`. In
  Angular: `<dz-calendar theme="night" scheme="dark" density="compact">`.

Without the theme CSS the calendar still works and reads in system colours —
but the ready-made families (`'slate'`…) are in that CSS: without it they
change nothing. In a shadow root, load the theme CSS *inside* that root (the
document's sheets do not reach it); `defineTheme` themes are put there by the
calendar itself. `THEME_NAMES` (exported) lists them; an unknown `theme`,
`scheme` or `density` is refused with a RangeError.

Every part, state and token you may rely on is listed in
`docs/styling.md` — the contract (a rename there is a major version).

## 2. Change anything — your rules always win

All of the calendar's CSS lives in two cascade layers, `dzcalendar.base` then
`dzcalendar.theme`. **Any rule of yours outside a layer wins over both,
whatever its specificity** — no `!important`, no copying our selectors:

```css
.dz-ev { border-radius: 0; }          /* square events */
.dz-toolbar { display: none; }        /* your own header (see CalendarController) */
```

(Cascade layers: Chrome 99, Safari 15.4, Firefox 97.) One exception: while
an event is dragged, the grabbing cursor is `!important` in the base layer.

### Beside a CSS framework

The calendar is built on no framework — plain CSS. What matters is the
page's **global reset**, which touches every element:

| Your page | Reset | Do |
|---|---|---|
| Tailwind CSS v4 | in `@layer base` | `@import '@dzcalendar/theme/tailwind.css';` before `@import 'tailwindcss';` |
| Tailwind CSS v3 | unlayered preflight | `cssLayers: false` + `@import '@dzcalendar/theme/tailwind3.css';` after `@tailwind base;` |
| Bootstrap 5, normalize.css, older CSS | unlayered | `cssLayers: false` + `@dzcalendar/theme/unlayered.css` |
| Plain modern CSS | none | nothing |

- **Tailwind's utilities from the calendar's tokens**: after `@import
  'tailwindcss'`, `@import '@dzcalendar/theme/tailwind-theme.css'` gives
  `bg-dz-accent`, `text-dz-fg`, `text-dz-muted`, `border-dz-border`,
  `bg-dz-raised`, `rounded-dz`… that follow the calendar's theme and scheme
  (inside a calendar; elsewhere set the `--dz-*` tokens yourself). The
  other way, a rule of yours: `.dz-cal { --dz-accent:
  var(--color-emerald-600); }`.
- **All of the look yours**: `look: 'none'` keeps the structure and drops
  the calendar's colours, borders, radii, fonts and shadows; your Tailwind
  classes go on its parts through `hooks.<element>.class`
  (`playground/tailwind.html` shows both, checked in Chrome).
- Layered (the default), the calendar's sheet is appended, so its layers come
  after any the page declared first (Tailwind 4's `base`): the preflight does
  not reset it. `tailwind.css` also puts it *before* Tailwind's utilities, so
  utilities on your own markup inside the calendar win.
- `cssLayers: false` (in Angular `provideDzCalendar({ cssLayers: false })`;
  the first calendar of a document decides): the same CSS outside any layer,
  inserted first. Its class selectors outweigh a reset's `*` and element
  rules; a rule of yours of the same weight, written after, wins.
- Checked in Chrome against the real Tailwind 3 preflight, Bootstrap 5.3
  reboot and Tailwind 4's layered preflight (`npm run test:browser`): every
  element of a week, a month and a list keeps the borders, paddings, margins
  and colours it has on a bare page. The one thing a reset still changes is a
  pointer cursor on events (they are `role="button"`).

**Under a Content-Security-Policy without inline styles** (`injectStyles:
false`): include `DZ_CSS`, `LIST_CSS`, `MULTIMONTH_CSS` (from their entries)
and, for a `defineTheme` theme, `themeCss('clinic')` in your own stylesheet. With an unstyled calendar (`look: 'none'`), give each of them through `lookGuardedCss(…)` (from `@dzcalendar/dom` or `@dzcalendar/dom/toolkit`).

**In a shadow root**, load the theme CSS inside the root; its sizes are on `:root, :host`.

## 3. Change the colours — tokens

The palette is shared with tzslot (`--tz-*`), so a page using both libraries
sets it once. The calendar's own tokens are `--dz-*`.

| Token | What |
|---|---|
| `--tz-bg`, `--tz-bg-raised` | backgrounds (page, raised: popovers, outside days) |
| `--tz-fg`, `--tz-fg-muted` | text, secondary text |
| `--tz-border` | lines |
| `--tz-accent`, `--tz-accent-fg` | accent (today, selected view, focus) and the text on it |
| `--tz-danger`, `--tz-warning` | refusals; clock-change marks |
| `--tz-radius`, `--tz-font` | corner radius, font |
| `--dz-today-bg`, `--dz-now` | today's column/cell; the current-time line |
| `--dz-event-bg`, `--dz-event-fg`, `--dz-event-accent` | events (by default derived from the accent or the event's tone) |
| `--dz-tone-<name>` | named event tones (`tone: 'green'` on an event) |
| `--dz-height`, `--dz-minute`, `--dz-bar-height`, `--dz-gutter-width` | sizes |
| `--dz-event-radius` | an event's corners (else `--dz-radius`, then tzslot's `--tz-radius`) |
| `--dz-on-tone`, `--dz-tone-<name>-on` | the text on a solid event (`eventStyle: 'solid'`): the theme's, or a tone's own — give one with a pale tone of yours |
| `--dz-allday-max` | how tall the all-day row grows before it scrolls |

```css
:root { --tz-accent: #0a7d5a; }      /* any family follows: the page first */
.dz-cal { --dz-radius: 2px; }
```

**The page first.** A family (ready-made or `defineTheme`) gives *defaults*
(`--dzp-*`); the calendar reads `--dz-x`, else the page's `--tz-x` (set on
`:root` or any ancestor), else the family's, else a system colour. So a
`--tz-accent` on `:root` recolours a calendar in `'slate'` too. The flip side:
a page loading tzslot's theme (which sets `--tz-*` on `:root`) shows tzslot's
palette whatever family is chosen. The palette is resolved on `.dz-cal`: set
`--tz-*` on the calendar or an ancestor, not on an event (events have
`--dz-event-*` and tones).

A value may be a `light-dark(light, dark)` pair where the browser supports it
(Safari 17.5+); a family's own light and dark need no such support.

## 4. A theme of your own

```ts
import { defineTheme } from '@dzcalendar/dom';
defineTheme('clinic', {
  accent: ['#0a7d5a', '#3ddc97'],          // [light, dark]
  bg: ['#ffffff', '#0f1915'],
  radius: '4px',
  tones: { urgent: ['#b91c1c', '#f87171'] },
});
createCalendar(host, { theme: 'clinic' });
```

It is injected in the `dzcalendar.theme` layer (outside any layer with
`cssLayers: false`), so your plain CSS still wins, and so does a `--tz-*` of
your page. Only the tokens listed above are accepted; values are checked (no
`;`, `{`, `url(` …). Defined again, calendars using it follow at once, in
shadow roots too.
In SCSS, the theme's variables are `!default`:
`@use '@dzcalendar/theme/dzcalendar' with ($accent: (#0a7d5a, #3ddc97));`.

## 5. Calendars of the dates

- `displayCalendar: 'islamic-umalqura'` writes titles, day numbers and labels
  in that calendar (any Intl calendar: `persian`, `hebrew`…). Data and grids
  stay Gregorian.
- `secondaryCalendar: 'islamic-umalqura'` shows that calendar's day beside
  each date (its month on the 1st), in headings and in what a screen reader
  says; it is not shown when it is the calendar already displayed. For an
  Arabic Hijri calendar with the Gregorian date beside it:
  `{ locale: 'ar-SA', displayCalendar: 'islamic-umalqura', secondaryCalendar: 'gregory' }`
  (write `displayCalendar` explicitly: engines differ on `ar-SA`'s default).
- Titles name every month of the display calendar the period covers (a
  Gregorian month in Hijri reads "Rabiʻ II – Jumada I 1448 AH"). Week numbers
  stay ISO/locale weeks. Umm al-Qura through Intl is the civil table, not the
  sighting-based dates of Ramadan and the Eids. A calendar Intl does not
  support is refused (RangeError).
- Browser baseline: Safari / iOS 15.4, Chrome 99, Firefox 97 (cascade
  layers). Light and dark need no `light-dark()`: each family's two palettes
  are plain values switched by `scheme`, `[data-theme]` and
  `prefers-color-scheme`. Where `color-mix()` is missing (Safari before 16.2),
  tints (events, today, outside days) fall back to the raised background.
  With `cssLayers: false` the CSS also works before cascade layers.

## 6. Words

See `docs/i18n.md`: English and French built in, Arabic, Spanish and German as
imports (`import '@dzcalendar/dom/locales/ar'`), `messages: { today: '…' }` to
change any word, `defineLocale` for a new language.

## 7. Printing

The theme's print sheet prints what scrolls whole, in colour; call
`cal.preparePrint()` (or set `autoPrint: true`) so everything is mounted and
no event hides behind "+N".

---

<!-- docs/migrating-from-fullcalendar.md -->

# Moving from FullCalendar

Two tools, used together:

- **`dz-migrate`** (`@dzcalendar/migrate`, a development tool) rewrites the
  code: imports, plugins, `new Calendar(...)`, the common calls, Angular's
  `<full-calendar>`. What needs a person is marked `// dz-migrate:`.
- **`@dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar`** translates the options object at run
  time: the application keeps its FullCalendar options and callbacks.

```sh
npm install -D @dzcalendar/migrate
npx dz-migrate src              # what would change
npx dz-migrate src --write      # rewrite
npm install @dzcalendar/core @dzcalendar/dom @dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar @dzcalendar/theme
npm uninstall @fullcalendar/core @fullcalendar/daygrid …   # every @fullcalendar/* package
```

## What `dz-migrate` rewrites

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `import { Calendar } from '@fullcalendar/core'` | `import { createFromFullCalendar } from '@dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar'` |
| `new Calendar(el, options)` | `createFromFullCalendar(el, options).calendar` |
| `calendar.render()` | removed (drawn when made) |
| `next()`, `prev()`, `today()` | `navigate('next' \| 'prev' \| 'today')` |
| `changeView(v)` | `update({ view: v })` |
| `refetchEvents()`, `unselect()`, `destroy()` | `refetch()`, `select(null)`, `destroy()` |
| types (`CalendarOptions`, `EventClickArg`, `EventApi`…) | the same names from `@dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar` |
| plugins (`daygrid`, `timegrid`, `interaction`, `rrule`, `icalendar`, `resource*`) | removed: built in |
| `@fullcalendar/list`, `multimonth` | `import '@dzcalendar/dom/list'`, `'@dzcalendar/dom/multimonth'` |
| `@fullcalendar/timeline`, `resource-timeline` | `import '@dzcalendar/pro'` |
| `@fullcalendar/core/locales/ar` (`es`, `de`) | `import '@dzcalendar/dom/locales/ar'`; `locale: arLocale` → `locale: 'ar'` |
| Angular: `FullCalendarModule` | `DZ_CALENDAR, DzFullCalendar` |
| Angular: `<full-calendar [options]="o">` | `<dz-calendar [dzFullCalendar]="o">` |
| `Calendar` as a type | `CalendarInstance` from `@dzcalendar/dom` |
| `@fullcalendar/core/locales-all` | the Arabic, Spanish and German imports (English, French built in) |

Marked for a person: `select(start, end)` (here `select({ start, end, allDay })`), `gotoDate(d)` (`update({ date: Temporal.PlainDate.from(d) })`),
`addEvent(e)` (`run({ type: 'event.create', event })`), `getEventById`,
`getEvents` (`kernel.store.snapshot`), `setOption(k, v)` (`update({ … })`),
`on` / `off` (the callbacks), Angular's `getApi()` (the `CalendarController`).
Left and said: `import * as FC from '@fullcalendar/core'` (import the names).

## What the options become

See `docs/behaviors/fullcalendar-options.md`. In short: the same views,
dates and events, each in its zone. A time without a zone is read in the
calendar's zone, and said. Days count from Monday = 1. Colours become tones
(the colour is kept in `extendedProps.color`). Callbacks receive plain
objects (`event.start` is a `Date`); a refused move is undone with
`revert()`. The height is CSS (`--dz-height`).

`createFromFullCalendar(el, options)` returns `{ calendar, problems,
detach }`: read `problems` once — every guess and every option without an
equivalent is there (`zone-guessed`, `compat-unsupported`).

## Before publication: installing from tarballs

Until the packages are on npm, they are tarballs (`npm run pack:local` in
this repository writes them to `packed/`). Install the whole closure, not
only what you import: `core`, `rrule`, `dom`, `theme`, and with the
translator `ical` and `compat-fullcalendar` — npm cannot fetch an internal
dependency it does not find beside the others. After replacing the tarballs
in an Angular application, empty its caches (`rm -rf .angular/cache
node_modules/.vite`): otherwise the dev server serves the old chunks and the
screen stays blank with `NG0919: Cannot read @Component metadata`, which is
not a circular dependency.

## What changes on the way

- **The zone.** FullCalendar's options rarely name one (theirs is the
  browser's); the calendar's then is the application's
  (`provideDzCalendar({ timeZone })`), never silently the browser's.
- **Every day's events.** FullCalendar shows them all unless `dayMaxEvents`
  says otherwise: so does the translation (`dayMaxLanes: null`, the weeks
  grow).
- **`eventDrop`, `eventResize`, `eventChange`, `eventAdd`, `eventRemove`**
  follow a person's change (a gesture, the keyboard, the menu, the editor);
  your own `calendar.run()` is not reported — theirs reports `addEvent` and
  `setProp` too. Persist from where your code makes the change.
- **The header.** `headerToolbar` is kept whole (`left` / `right` are
  `start` / `end`; `false`, no header) and `customButtons` with it (their
  `icon` becomes the class `fc-icon fc-icon-<name>`: bring its icon in your
  CSS). `prevYear` / `nextYear` are said and left out
  (`docs/behaviors/header-toolbar.md`).
- **Formats.** `titleFormat`, `dayHeaderFormat`, `slotLabelFormat`,
  `eventTimeFormat`, `listDayFormat`, `listDaySideFormat`,
  `dayPopoverFormat` keep their platform options (`formats`); their own keys
  (`meridiem`, `omitZeroMinute`…) and format functions are said. Without
  one, hours are the locale's ("09:00" in French, "9:00 AM" in English), not
  their compact "9a".
- **Custom views.** `views: { x: { type, duration, dayCount, dateIncrement,
  visibleRange } }` become ours by settings (`docs/custom-views.md`).
- **Dragging in.** `new Draggable(el, { itemSelector, eventData })` from
  their interaction plugin is the compat's (`import { Draggable } from
  '@dzcalendar/compat-fullcalendar'`; `dz-migrate` rewrites the import);
  `droppable`, `drop`, `eventReceive`, `eventLeave` keep their arguments
  (`draggedEl`, `revert`). `eventData.create: false` tells `drop` only.
  Natively: `makeDraggable` (`docs/behaviors/external-drag.md`).
- **Render hooks.** `<name>ClassNames`, `<name>Content`, `<name>DidMount`,
  `<name>WillUnmount` for the elements in `docs/behaviors/render-hooks.md`,
  with their arguments' names; a `ClassNames` function gets no `el`.
- **Types**: `view` is never null in the callbacks' arguments.
